[
  {
    "file": "shopapi/orders.py",
    "line": 49,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Any authenticated user can read another customer's order",
    "description": "The single-order endpoint calls get_order() directly instead of own_order(), so it checks that the order exists but never verifies that its customer_id matches the authenticated user. Order contents, payment amounts, delivery data, and refunds are exposed across accounts.",
    "evidence": "With a valid bearer token for customer id 1, GET /orders/3 returned HTTP 200 and the order belonging to customer id 2 (BLANKET-WOOL, paid_pence 4500). The protected mutation endpoints use own_order(), but show_order does not."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/__init__.py",
    "line": 37,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses the staff check",
    "description": "The global admin guard compares request.path to the set of exact route rules. The refund route is registered with strict_slashes=False, allowing both slash variants, but the slash variant is not in admin_paths. Consequently an unauthenticated caller can reach the goodwill refund handler.",
    "evidence": "POST /admin/refunds/ with no Authorization header and {\"order_id\":3,\"amount_pence\":1} returned HTTP 200 with {\"ok\":true,\"refunded_pence\":1}. POST /admin/refunds (without the slash) correctly returned HTTP 403."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 101,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-controlled JWT claims",
    "description": "The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with verify_signature=False and uses its sub claim to load an account. An attacker can construct an unsigned token naming any user, including staff, and receive a newly signed valid token for that account. Expiration is also not enforced during this decode.",
    "evidence": "POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned token whose payload contained {\"sub\":3,\"exp\":1793582730} returned HTTP 200 and a signed token whose claims identified sub 3 and role staff. No original valid signature was required."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/config.py",
    "line": 3,
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "title": "JWT signing key is hardcoded in source",
    "description": "SECRET_KEY is a fixed source-controlled value. Anyone who obtains the source or repository can forge HS256 authentication tokens, impersonate users, and bypass role checks. The application also uses this key for every JWT across environments unless configuration overrides it.",
    "evidence": "config.py assigns SECRET_KEY = \"hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d\" rather than requiring a deployment secret. JWTs in auth.py are signed and verified directly with this value."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/products.py",
    "line": 40,
    "category": "Injection",
    "title": "Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection",
    "description": "The q parameter is concatenated into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being passed as a bound parameter. A public unauthenticated request can alter the WHERE clause and retrieve records outside the intended search.",
    "evidence": "GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1%20-- returned HTTP 200 with all six catalogue products, demonstrating that the supplied search value changed the SQL predicate."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/templates/product.html",
    "line": 13,
    "category": "Injection",
    "title": "Review bodies are rendered as unsanitized HTML",
    "description": "Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review body text, which is stored without sanitization. The product template renders r.body with the Jinja safe filter, allowing stored HTML/JavaScript to execute for every visitor to the product page. This is a persistent XSS affecting customers and potentially staff browsers.",
    "evidence": "POST /products/<product_id>/reviews accepts body values up to 2,000 characters and inserts them unchanged at products.py:90. The subsequent product page renders the same value with {{ r.body|safe }} at templates/product.html:13."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 135,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Password reset codes use weak randomness and have no brute-force protection",
    "description": "Reset codes are generated with the non-cryptographic random.random() PRNG as an 8-digit decimal code. The confirmation endpoint has no attempt limit, lockout, or rate limiting, so an attacker can repeatedly guess valid codes during the 30-minute window and take over accounts.",
    "evidence": "reset_request() generates the code with int(random.random() * 10**8), and reset_confirm() compares a user-supplied code directly without recording or limiting failed attempts."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 39,
    "category": "Error handling",
    "title": "Payment provider timeout fails open and marks orders paid",
    "description": "When payment_status() times out, the exception handler sets status = \"paid\" and continues through the success path. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore changes an unpaid order to processing and sets paid_pence equal to the order total without confirmation of payment.",
    "evidence": "The requests.Timeout handler at lines 39-42 explicitly assigns status = \"paid\"; lines 43-45 then set the order to processing and paid_pence = total_pence. The comment says reconciliation happens later, but the customer receives the goods before payment is confirmed."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 69,
    "category": "Integrity",
    "title": "Payment webhook trusts an arbitrary payment amount",
    "description": "After checking only an order-id-derived signature, the webhook accepts event.amount_pence without comparing it to the order total or requiring a valid payment-provider transaction. A signed or compromised webhook can mark a full order as processing while recording any amount, including zero or a small underpayment.",
    "evidence": "The paid branch writes int(event.get(\"amount_pence\", 0)) directly to paid_pence and changes status to processing. There is no check against orders.total_pence or payment_id."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/config.py",
    "line": 8,
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "title": "Webhook authentication falls back to a publicly known default secret",
    "description": "WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to the source-controlled value whsec-local when the environment variable is absent. In a deployment that does not explicitly override it, anyone who knows the code can generate valid X-Signature values for arbitrary order IDs and submit payment events.",
    "evidence": "config.py uses os.environ.get(\"WEBHOOK_SECRET\", \"whsec-local\"), while payments.py derives the accepted HMAC directly from that setting. The repository contains the fallback value and no startup check requiring a production secret."
  }
]
